articles.title: PlayStation Plus Monthly Games for September 2026 Leak, Headlined by Sniper Elite: Resistance
articles.summary: September's PlayStation Plus monthly games lineup has leaked online ahead of Sony's official announcement.
articles.body:
September's PlayStation Plus monthly games lineup has leaked online ahead of Sony's official announcement.

As detailed by Dealabs ' ever-reliable billbilk-kun, next month's list of titles available to PlayStation Plus subscribers will include last year's Sniper Elite: Resistance, placing you behind the long gun barrel of a British agent infiltrating Nazi-occupied Europe in 1944.

"A solid stealth-based shooter," is how IGN's Sniper Elite: Resistance review described the game, affording it a 6/10 score. "It fails to set its sights high enough in order to pull off a truly spectacular execution," we added.

The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time

Released back in 2022, the classic Japanese role-playing game inspired Chained Echoes is next on the roster. Inspired by classics such as Secret of Mana, Chrono Trigger and Final Fantasy 4, this retro-feeling RPG proudly wears its influences on its sleeve — but is no worse off for doing so.

Lastly, there's Wobbly Life. This colorful open-world sandbox launched last year and lets you muck about with friends to complete jobs, earn money, and own houses. All three games will be available from September 1 to October 6.

As a reminder, you still have until September 1 to claim August's trio of titles for PS Plus members. Those offerings include Dying Light 2 Stay Human: Reloaded Edition, Big Walk and Signalis.

articles.title: The Simpsons Parodies Black Mirror in New Disney+ Special
articles.summary: Ahead of the Season 38 premiere, The Simpsons is returning to Disney+ for a special episode that lampoons Black Mirror. Check out our exclusive preview of "Yellow Mirror."
articles.body:
The Simpsons will soon return for a mind-boggling 38th Season on Fox. But if you can't wait that long, you're in luck. The series is about to drop its latest exclusive episode on Disney+, and we've got an exclusive early look.

Check out the slideshow gallery below to see exclusive new images from "Yellow Mirror":

The Simpsons: "Yellow Mirror" Image Gallery

"Yellow Mirror" isn't the first Simpsons special to be exclusive to Disney+, but it is notable for being a full-length episode rather than a short in the vein of "The Simpsons in Plusaversary." As the title suggests, this episode acts as a spoof of Netflix's popular sci-fi anthology series Black Mirror. It features two tales linked by a common dystopian technology theme.

Here's the official description for "Yellow Mirror":

A defective lamp reveals a heartbreaking truth about what Homer believes is reality, and an AI-powered tablet befriends and controls Maggie. The Simpsons struggle to find the light through two dark tales of the curious and bizarre in this Disney+ exclusive.

"Yellow Mirror" will premiere on Disney+ on Wednesday, August 26.

In other The Simpsons news, Bart Simpson voice actress Nancy Cartwright believes the series will ultimately end with Season 40 . The show also recently returned to Fortnite, where fans could collect a Simpsons-style John Wick skin .

Fans were also recently given new hope about the long-awaited return of The Simpsons: Hit & Run , with Matt Groening saying, "I think the original game is coming back in some form."

articles.title: KFC Reveals the Oreo Chicken Burger, and We're Both Revolted and Intrigued
articles.summary: Has capitalism gone too far? KFC China has just revealed the Oreo Original Recipe Chicken Burger, and we can't help but be intrigued.
articles.body:
If you're a fan of strange and unholy fast food concoctions, then you'll definitely want to see what the crazed scienticians at KFC and Nabisco have concocted. Fresh off the reveal of their fried chicken-flavored Oreo cookies in China, the two companies have reversed that fusion to create the Oreo Original Recipe Chicken Burger.

This bizarre collab was revealed by KFC China on Weibo ( via Dexerto ). It looks every bit as strange as it sounds. The sandwich starts off ordinarily enough, with a fried chicken patty and lettuce, but it's topped with brown mashed potatoes dusted in cookie crumbles and placed between two Oreo cookie-flavored buns.

Like any good fast food mash-up, we can't decide if we're grossed out by this creation or deeply intrigued. Either way, American foodies shouldn't count on being able to try the Oreo Original Recipe Chicken Burger anytime soon. The sandwich is currently limited to the Chinese market only, with no indication of when or if it might come to the US.

Will you devour an Oreo Chicken Sandwich if given the opportunity? Cast your vote in our poll below:

This is just the latest odd creation from the folks at Nabisco. Past Oreo cookie variants have included Post Malone Oreos , which featured swirled salted caramel and shortbread flavored cream squeezed between one golden and one chocolate Oreo wafer cookie, and Mario Oreos . And in perhaps the most unholy combination of them all, there's the Ritz Oreo .

articles.title: Marvel Tokon Devs Confess Regaining Trust After Fumbled PC Launch Will Be 'Extremely Challenging'
articles.summary: Arc System Works has apologized for Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls' PC launch and admitted it will be "extremely difficult" to regain player trust.
articles.body:
Arc System Works has apologized for the troubled PC launch of Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls , and admitted it will now be "extremely difficult" to regain player trust.

Producer Takeshi Yamanaka offered a post-mortem on the release of the studio's new superhero fighting game during an interview with VGC . He noted that, when it comes to the content itself, fans have mostly nice things to say about Marvel Tokon, but the positivity isn't being shared by users across all platforms.

"They’re playing matches every day, they’re in training mode, they’re coming up with new combos, and we see them posting those on social media," Yamanaka said. "However, at the same time, unfortunately, in the PC version of the game, there have been in-game issues experienced by many players, which we really apologise to the player base for all of these problems."

Marvel Tokon brought tag-team gameplay to PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S August 6, 2026. While reviewers largely lobbed high scores its way (IGN gave it a 9/10 ), those on PC instead took to Steam to leave reviews of their own.

Arc System Works' new fighting game plummeted to "Mixed" reviews in all languages less than 24 hours after launch as players reported stuttering issues and forced PlayStation sign-in requirements. The weekend following its release on PC was only plagued by more negativity as the problems persisted, with the only message from the studio at the time being its promise to "investigate" reports of "performance issues." The state of Marvel Tokon on PC reportedly was so bad that even famed fighting game community content creator Maximilian Christiansen (a.k.a. Maximilian Dood) uninstalled the game in front of thousands of livestream viewers .

Arc System Works was able to speedily push out an update the following Monday, fixing many of the performance issues players had reported. But while Steam reviews have slightly rebounded, it's clear there's a long road ahead not only for Marvel Tokon but for the studio itself.

Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls Knights of Doom State of Play June 2026 Reveal Trailer - Screenshots

Yamanaka said "the team is hard at work to continue working on resolving remaining issues," noting two of the patches that have arrived since that early August release date. He also admitted that getting the Marvel fighting game in tip-top shape is only part of the battle.

"I do think that it's an extremely challenging task that we need to undertake," he said when asked about regaining trust, "where we sincerely want to put all of our effort forward to create an environment where the players can experience this game that we’ve worked so hard to create, and that we do have a lot of confidence that the game itself will be really fun for them."

Yamanaka again apologized for Marvel Tokon on PC after it "created a lot of trouble for the players." He and the rest of the team are hoping the community will stick around not only for those incoming fixes but more for the game itself, too.

"I would like to just say that I truly appreciate every single player who purchased the game around the launch," he added. "And to some players on the PC who were kind enough to purchase the game, but then they experienced these issues and were unable to play the game in its best way, and maybe left the game for the moment or even refunded. I would just like to express my sincere apologies for all of those issues that they’ve experienced.

"I do feel that it will not be an easy task at all to regain the trust that we've lost from this. However, this is an issue that we're facing head-on, and we’re trying to tackle it directly to try to continue working with all that we have and to provide an environment where players will be able to smoothly experience the game.

The Arc System Works producer continued, saying, "I feel that is the most that we can do." As additional updates are launched, he said, "all we can do is do our best and pray that that sentiment will reach the player base."

Either way, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is just getting started. DLC content is confirmed to be in the works, with Phoenix Cyclops already announced as a playable character set to join the roster this fall. Dataminers uncovered five more potential fighters earlier this month .

articles.title: GeForce Now is getting support for the Steam Controller
articles.summary: Nvidia’s GeForce Now cloud gaming service will officially support Valve’s Steam Machine and Steam Controller starting later this year. Nvidia also announced that EA and Ubisoft will support RTX Spark.
articles.body: Nvidia’s GeForce Now cloud gaming service will officially support Valve’s Steam Controller and Steam Machine starting later this year. With Steam Controller support, you’ll be able to play games with Valve’s great new gamepad when using the GeForce Now app on your Steam Deck or Steam Machine. If you’re using GeForce Now on Windows or macOS, support for the Steam Controller is coming “later,” Nvidia says. GeForce Now is getting a few other upgrades, too. Nvidia will soon add new DLSS 4.5 controls for DLSS Super Resolution, Dynamic Frame Generation, and Ray Reconstruction. (Ray Reconstruction is also officially launching for RTX GPUs in early access.) The previously-announced GOG single sign on is now available. The service will come to more of Amazon’s Fire TV Sticks “later this year,” and you’ll be able to buy a subscription through Amazon. And as of last week, you can officially use GeForce Now on Firefox. [Media: Nvidia’s Gamescom announcements also include news for its upcoming RTX Spark chip family: EA, Embark, and Ubisoft are planning to support the chip, which is set to launch this fall, with games like EA Sports F1 25, Apex Legends, Arc Raiders, and Anno 117: Pax Romana. EA is also working on native support for its Javelin Anticheat technology for the company’s “biggest multiplayer games.” Nvidia also shared details about 007 First Light’s path tracing update launching in September, upgrades to RTX Remix, and more, and you can read about everything that’s new in the company’s blog post.

articles.title: RoboCop TV Show Casts Dan Stevens as Its Star
articles.summary: Prime Video's RoboCop TV show has reportedly cast Dan Stevens as its star.
articles.body:
UPDATE AUGUST 25, 2026: RoboCop star Dan Stevens has confirmed he's joined the Prime Video show with a social media post.

Stevens took to Instagram to share a video about the announcement, confirming his involvement. He didn't have much to add, but judging by the action figure behind him, it's safe to say he's excited.

"Buzz buzz..." he said. "Dead or alive, you're coming with me."

ORIGINAL STORY: Prime Video's RoboCop TV show has reportedly cast Dan Stevens as its star.

The Downton Abbey star has officially boarded the untitled RoboCop reboot series, according to Deadline . Stevens will play a new version of the cop-turned-robot, Alex Murphy.

Amazon MGM reportedly had its eye on Stevens early in the casting process. While he might be best known as Matthew Crawley, he's also appeared in projects like The Guest, the live-action Beauty and the Beast, the animated Among Us series, and more. The original Alex Murphy was played by Peter Weller, who returned to reprise the role across many RoboCop sequels and spinoffs.

Here's the official logline for the show: "A giant tech conglomerate convinces the city to place a powerful robot on its police force — a robot implanted with the consciousness of a beloved, fallen officer."

Amazon greenlit its Prime Video RoboCop revival in July, though it's said to have been in some form of development since the company acquired MGM back in 2022. Peter Ocko (Moonhaven, Lodge 49) is attached as showrunner, writer, and co-executive producer.

Blumhouse Atomic Monster's Michael Clear, Rob Hackett, and The Conjuring's James Wan are all involved as executive producers, too, with Danielle Bozzone overseeing for the company. Original RoboCop writers Ed Neumeier and Michael Miner are also executive producers.

"What Paul Verhoeven created in 1987 was decades ahead of its time, and its questions about technology, identity, and who corporations really serve have only grown more urgent,” Wan said in July. "With Peter’s distinctive vision and bold approach to storytelling, and alongside Ed and our partners at Amazon MGM Studios, we’re working to honor what made the original iconic and highlight its relevancy in this modern, tech-driven world, while building something unmistakably new for a global audience."

Outside of that aforementioned logline and the promise to deliver an eight-episode series, we know little about how RoboCop will revitalize an '80s action icon for modern audiences. Although it's without a firm release date or even any sort of window to look forward to, picking up Stevens just one month after the greenlighting process suggests the ball is rolling fast for now.

For more, you can read IGN's review for the RoboCop Criterion Collection release . You can also check out what we thought of the character's latest video game in our RoboCop: Rogue City review .

articles.title: Why Even Consider a Projector When Costco Has an Excellent 100" Hisense 4K TV for Just $1,500?
articles.summary: This massive TV even comes with an extended 5 year warranty.
articles.body:
As both an avid tech enthusiast and die-hard deal hunter, I'm a huge fan of Hisense's QD7 TV lineup. The QD7 offers premium features that will sure to please both movie watchers and console gamers at a price point that caters to the budget-conscious. It's available in several sizes, but the garganutan 100" model is exclusively sold at Costco.

For Labor Day, the 100" Hisense QD7 4K Hi-QLED Fire TV is on sale for just $1,4997.97 after a $300 iff instant discount and free delivery to your door. That's not all. Costco is throwing in an extended 3 year AllState warranty on top of Hisense's 2 year warranty for a total of 5 years. That's incredible considering most TVs come with a piddly one year.

100" Hisense QD7 4K Hi-QLED Fire TV for $1,499.99

I love big TVs. And when I mean big, I don't mean 65" or 77". In my eyes, those are average sizes. I mean 90" and higher. I used to own a pricey projector setup back in the day and even had a custom retractable projector screen. After I got a big TV, I did away with my setup and I haven't looked back. Unless you're looking for a significantly bigger size than 100" - like a 150" setup for a dedicated home theater room - you should consider doing the same.

Costco's Hisense QD7 TV won't disappoint for streaming your favorite TV shows, movies, and sports. Apart from the screen size, which needs no explanation for its awesome-ness, the QD7 delivers a great 4K HDR picture with support for Dolby Vision, HDR10, HDR10+, and HLG formats. Hisense's proprietary Hi-QLED panel offers more vibrant and accurate colors and higher peak HDR brightness than traditional LED LCD TVs. The QD7 is also a very bright TV - much brighter than OLED TVs - and punches through even in bright, sunlit rooms.

Gamers will be happy to know that the QD7 is ready for 4K console gaming and is a great complement to the PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X console. That's because it's equipped with a native 144Hz panel with AMD FreeSync Premium variable refresh rate. It syncs with games running in 4K at up to 144fps and virtually eliminates stuttering or screen tearing you'd see otherwise with mis-matched frame rate and refresh rate.

If you're familar with the Amazon Fire TV interface or you're invested in the Amazon Alexa ecosystem, then the smart interface on the Hisense QD7 should feel familiar to you. You'll have access to pretty much every streaming app on the market and you'll be able to control your TV through your remote, any mobile device that can download the Fire TV app, or with voice control via your Echo smart home device.

The vast majority of TVs come with the industry standard one year warranty. Hisense provides a two year warranty. As if that wasn't good enough, Costco's three year warranty extension - for up to 5 years total - means your TV will be covered for longer than most of the other major home electronics or appliances in your house. That kind of product assurance is rare and universally welcomed, especially when it comes at no extra charge.

Stay tuned for more Labor Day sales as the deals start to drop this week.

articles.title: gamescom Opening Night Live 2026: Everything Announced
articles.summary: Opening Night Live 2026 is upon us, and with it comes the promise of big new gameplay reveals, plenty of new trailers, and a long list of announcements. Check out IGN's live report, direct from gamescom.
articles.body:
Opening Night Live 2026 is over for another year, and it brought plenty of announcements, new trailers, and news on upcoming games. We've got all the reveals that matter right here, rounded up below.

Highlights include The Witcher 3 Remastered, The Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past, the new trailer for Final Fantasy VII Revelation, and the surprise drop of Crimson Desert Enhanced.

Check below for live updates straight from Opening Night Live!

ONL is over for another year! The Witcher 3 remaster is the definite standout moment, but I'm also looking forward to No Law and Crazy Tazi. What was your favorite reveal?

And finally, we got a look at The Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, which is due out in 2027. Geralt is back! CD Projekt also announced that the previous two expansions are now free. Like, right now! Much more on The Witcher 3 - Songs of the Past right here .

Wow! This is perhaps the biggest reveal of ONL: a remaster of CD Projekt's The Witcher 3! It's a free upgrade for all The Witcher 3 owners, and is out September 29, 2026. Much more on The Witcher 3 Remastered here .

And here's a big one! At ONL we got a new look at Final Fantasy VII Revelation, the final entry in the Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy. Director Naoki Hamaguchi took to the stage to confirm a spring 2027 release window and intro a new trailer, below.

In the trailer, enormous guardians called Weapons emerge to defend a world in crisis. Making no distinction between friend and foe, the Weapons wreak catastrophic destruction upon the planet and its people. Upon desert sands, in mid-air dogfights and at the bottom of the sea, Cloud and his fellow heroes must stand against the colossal Weapons even as they toil to save the world from Sephiroth. A late-game element of the original Final Fantasy VII, the Weapons return in reimagined glory as standout battles in Final Fantasy VII Revelation, some of which appear in ultra-challenging endgame battles as an homage to their original forms.

The new trailer also showcases the powerful new Summon Typhon and open-world exploration via parachute, grappling hook and Chocobo mounts, plus Cloud and Tifa in their Warrior and Black Mage FITS. New to Final Fantasy VII Revelation, the FITS system introduces unique outfits that bestow new abilities and greater heights of power, with specialized roles evoking classic Final Fantasy jobs.

Much more on Final Fantasy VII Revelation right here .

Tarae: The Unbound made its first public appearance at ONL, introducing its world and gameplay. The game is set in an Eastern dark fantasy world, with Eastern-inspired cinematic visuals and narration from Agasa introducing the game’s world and story before transitioning into a hero confronting a great calamity. The trailer then moves into gameplay, featuring powerful abilities and high-pressure boss encounters.

The Defiant is a story-driven shooter set in the rarely explored Asian theatre of World War II, built in Unreal Engine 5 and featuring cinematic visuals alongside replayable tactical combat. It's described as the first major war game centred on China's War of Resistance against Japan. Expect a launch on PC, Xbox Series X and S, and PlayStation 5.

Developer and publisher Morefun Studios announced that Roco Kingdom — the multiplayer open-world creature-collector and newest entry in the massively popular Chinese franchise — will now launch globally. Roco Kingdom is coming to Windows PC, PlayStation, Xbox, and mobile devices (iOS and Android) globally, with a release date to be announced at a later date.

Friday Sundae's musical mystery sees players inherit a crumbling English hotel and restore it by day, while battling ghosts by night alongside a sardonic cat and a talking power tool. Expect a release later this year.

More animal games! And more rats, I think. Action rabbit here we go! Zoopunk is the Metroidvania action game by TiGames, a Tencent Games-backed studio.

I'm not sure what this trailer is, but it's certainly... something! Pony Island 2 Panda Circus is out April 27, 2027.

We got our first look at Ontos, the next game from Frictional Games, developer of Amnesia. It stars Swedish actor Stellan Skarsgård, and there are lots of rats in it! Ontos is due out on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X and S in 2027.

I'm really looking forward to No Law, the next game from the developers of The Ascent. It's a first-person Cyberpunk-style game where you go around causing havoc in an open-world city. The kick is a big deal in this one. It's due out in 2027.

Ubisoft announced Heroes of Might & Magic 3 remake with a cinematic trailer that also includes gameplay. It's a modern reimagining of the turn-based strategy classic, developed by Ubisoft China studios in Chengdu and Shanghai. Expect a launch in 2027 on Ubisoft+, Xbox Series X and S, PlayStation and PC through Ubisoft Connect, Steam, and the Epic Games Store.

Path of Exile 2 has its full 1.0 release set for December 11, 2026. Grinding Gear Games' free-to-play action RPG will introduce the Duelist, a sword-focused melee class, and add the remaining campaign Acts with the 1.0 launch. The new class debuted in a fresh trailer, below.

Finally, LEGO Skylines is announced! Iceflake Studios' LEGO Skylines is a cozy, customizable city-builder where players begin with a single plot and grow it into a thriving metropolis, balancing roads, electricity, food, water, public services, and citizen happiness as they unlock new buildings and features. It's due out on PC via Steam, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, and Nintendo Switch 2.

This new third-person co-op action game sees you play as a humaoid dog. Really. Independent developer and publisher Octopus Panic announced Gravhounds, a new 1-4-player co-op action builder coming to early access on PC and Xbox Series X and S on November 2, 2026, and available day one with Xbox Game Pass. The announcement trailer, below, showcases the game's chaotic, physics-driven mayhem, tasking players with dropping into hostile planets as a pack, building defensive fortifications, and extracting with valuable resources before becoming alien chow.

During ONL, Saber Interactive revealed the new story trailer for Turok: Origins, the fast-paced, dinosaur-hunting sci-fi shooter launching in spring 2027 on PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S and Nintendo Switch 2.

I'm really looking forward to Crazy Taxi coming back! The new trailer for Crazy Taxi: World Tour offers a first look at the multiplayer modes, where the city becomes a shared playground where rival drivers compete for passengers. The trailer also confirms the return of fan favorites Gena, B.D. Joe, and Gus.

Crazy Taxi: World Tour is set to release in 2027 on Xbox Series X and S, Xbox on PC, Steam, PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2.

RedOctane Games announced its upcoming rhythm title, Stage Tour, launches on December 10, 2026 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC. The new trailer features Mötley Crüe’s 'Kickstart My Heart.'

Focus Entertainment and Saber Interactive confirmed the release date for Road Kings, "the next-gen truck simulator," with a brand-new trailer. Road Kings invites players to take the driver’s seat of a 40-ton semi, delivering goods across the American South while facing disasters both natural and man-made.

Players build their own trucking empire from the ground up, starting with nothing but a truck. Every job completed and every mile driven shapes your reputation: go from a lone rookie to the owner of your own company built job by job, delivery by delivery.

Road Kings launches March 11, 2027, on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X and S.

After a Mewgenics musical performance from Matthias Bossi, Carla Kihlsteadt and Geoff Pearlman from Ridiculon, we got confirmation of a console release date on PS5, Nintendo Switch 2, and Xbox Series X and S: September 8.

We’re very excited to have a special Mewgenics musical performance at #OpeningNightLive ! Give it up for Matthias Bossi, Carla Kihlsteadt and Geoff Pearlman from Ridiculon performing Guillotina! pic.twitter.com/wwIDmuYvya — Summer Game Fest (@summergamefest) August 25, 2026

We’re very excited to have a special Mewgenics musical performance at #OpeningNightLive ! Give it up for Matthias Bossi, Carla Kihlsteadt and Geoff Pearlman from Ridiculon performing Guillotina! pic.twitter.com/wwIDmuYvya

Here's another game from HoYoverse: Petit Planet, a cosy life sim where you enjoy slow, fulfilling days on your very own planet.

Afterworld is a new grand strategy game from Paradox all about restoring the might of America after an apocalyptic event. It's Paradox Development Studio’s first original setting in a decade.

Set in a procedurally generated North American wasteland, players guide a small band of survivors as they secure food, water, and shelter, rediscover lost technology, and build a continent-spanning empire.

Players will define the laws and values of their society, navigate moral crises, negotiate or fight with rival tribes, and unlock advances through a dynamic Ideas Tree shaped by what they discover and experience.

The strategic sandbox supports both competitive multiplayer and co-op, with emergent stories, shifting resources, ancient technology, and immortal pre-Fall leaders known as the Ancients.

Expect a launch at some point on PC via Steam.

NC’s Aion 2 has an October 5 release date on PC (Steam and PURPLE) in North America, South America, Europe, and Asia. Before launch, NC will conduct a 'Launch Scale Test' on September 17-18, building an environment similar to the actual service to check server and infrastructure stability, while also giving players the opportunity to experience the game before its official launch.

NC will then give players who have signed up for the Founder’s Pack five days of Early Access gameplay from September 30 to October 4, before the official launch October 5.

Yes, you read that right: Snoop Dog is coming to Hitman. Why not? The rap legend joins the World of Assassination as Dr. Cyrus Cane, an eccentric entrepreneur renowned for his wide-ranging and unconventional business ventures. In this new mission, Agent 47 sets his sights on eliminating Cane. His newest venture, Morsizzles, is a cookie product poised for a worldwide launch and millions in profits as buzz over its addictive taste spreads across social media and investment circles. However, beneath the hype lies a darker truth: an investigation has surfaced evidence of cover-ups linked to several deaths during internal product testing. To stop the launch and fulfil the contract, Dr. Cane must be permanently removed as the face of Morsizzles and the product must disappear.

Ukraine-based developer 4A Games took to the stage to intro Metro 2039 with a brand new gameplay trailer, showing the new voiced protagonist known only as The Stranger. The two-minute trailer, titled Renegade, was captured entirely in-game, and shows The Stranger using a mix of stealth and combat to infiltrate a Novoreich-occupied Moscow.

This trailer gives players just a taste of the hauntingly beautiful hand-crafted environments waiting to be explored, from the realities of daily life in Sevastopolskaya station to the deadly irradiated surface of Moscow, and thrilling FPS stealth action gameplay made possible by harnessing the proprietary power of the 4A Engine.

Metro 2039 is due out February 2027 across PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, and PC via Steam and Epic Games Store.

Elementa Games’ Unreal Engine 5-powered open-world action RPG, Silver Palace, got a brand-new trailer at ONL, revealing a first look at the game’s multiplayer and brand-new story elements. This detective adventure is currently in development for PC, mobile, and PlayStation 5.

What if Assassin's Creed had hoverboards? 1001 Threads of Mizan looks a bit like that. Developed and published by MBC Game Studio, which is made up of developers from BioWare, Hi-Rez, Ubisoft Montréal, and Bungie, 1001 Threads of Mizan is an action-adventure set in the world of One Thousand and One Nights. It's an Arabian fantasy title that sees players soar through the skies on flying carpets through drop-in, drop out co-op to explore and take down colossal bosses together.

Resident Evil star Maggie Robertson came out on stage to introduce third-person single-player action-adventure game Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons. The extended gameplay reveal showed off exploration, traversal puzzle-solving, and plenty of dialogue. Combat involves lots of magic, teleportation, and swordplay. The action looks a little clunky, but the magic system looks interesting. It's due out 2027 across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X and S. Here's the official blurb from Wizards of the Coast:

Warlock is set in a dark fantasy open world inspired by Dungeons & Dragons where magic is a tool that players will use creatively across systemic combat and exploration. Developed by Invoke Studios, the game places players in the role of Kaatri, a veteran weapons master who makes a pact to wield otherworldly magic against dark powers. The role of Kaatri is performed by the award-winning Tricia Helfer (Battlestar Galactica, Lucifer). Warlock empowers players to use magic to overcome a wide range of challenges. In exploration, every spell is a key that unlocks new paths and possibilities in a beautiful yet unsettling world. When facing enemies, magic and melee combine for a combat experience that is both tactical and visceral.

The Warlock gameplay reveal starts off by revealing a brand-new character: Tasha. Maggie Robertson plays the role of Tasha, who acts as Kaatri’s patron and source of power. Tasha teaches Kaatri to sense Raw Magic, power hidden throughout Darkon that lets her expand and transform her magical ability.

From there, the reveal shows how magic allows players to read and reshape the world. Kaatri turns the environment, enemy positioning and even the weather into tactical opportunities, chaining spells together.

Archetype Entertainment's Mass Effect-style Exodus has a new trailer and a release date: April 7, 2027. That's for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, Steam, and Epic Games Store. The new cinematic gameplay trailer reveals more of Salt, an Awakened octopus mercenary and bounty hunter who joins Jun's journey as a companion. During the video, fans are given another glimpse into the game's combat and universe. Much more on Exodus here .

Darksiders developer Airship Syndicate announced Dust Origins, a new isometric action game that's dripping with sci-fi cool. It reminds me of The Ascent, which is fantastic.

We got a good look at the real-time strategy game, Game of Thrones: War for Westeros, via a new gameplay trailer. John Snow is in it! It's due out early 2027. More on Game of Thrones: War for Westeros right here .

PUBG: DED.NET is a new PvP FPS from PUBG STUDIOS set in Cascadia in 1996, a fictional region inspired by the American Pacific Northwest. It introduces a darker new setting for the PUBG franchise built around character-driven combat, shifting match conditions, and roguelite progression across multi-match runs. Players can now also register for the upcoming closed beta.

Led by Ubisoft Montpellier and Ubisoft Milan, Rayman Legends Retold builds on the charm of the original 2013 game, now brought to life with 3D visuals, a brand-new story, and fully voiced cinematics. The new trailer is below.

Mega Man Dual Override, and a Mega Man skin for Pragmata!

We have a gorgeous-looking new game called Lofsong, from an indepent developer in Italy called Unrelated Games.

We have confirmation of Angela Sant'Albano as the new voice for lead character, Gwendolyn, alongside a new trailer. Sant'Albano played Grace Ashcroft in Resident Evil Requiem. Eclipse Glow Games' new trailer for its highly anticipated single-player action-adventure title, offers players a dramatic look at the emotional core of the game following the cataclysmic destruction of London as Gwendolyn mysteriously inherits the mystical power of King Arthur.

In the trailer, a distraught Gwendolyn considers her new reality amid the ash of a ruinous London before being encouraged by the legendary Guinevere to harness the power of the Fog - a power only King Arthur once wielded - to save both London and the otherworldly realm of Avalon from total annihilation. Embracing her destiny, Gwendolyn takes up the sword and learns to fight alongside powerful spectral knights; this new trailer debuts the legendary Sir Lancelot summoned by Gwendolyn to dispatch enemies in spectacular style.

Tides of Annihilation is currently being developed for PC via Steam and Epic Games Store, Xbox Series X and S, and PlayStation 5.

We got a new look at Silent Hill: Townfall, the next spinoff in Konami's horror franchise. The trailer below confirms the English cast, which includes Jovan Adepo, Terry O’Quinn, and Keiza Burrows. Emmy Award winner Terry O’Quinn (Lost, The Walking Dead: The Ones Who Live) joins the cast as Richard, an enigmatic character who summons protagonist Simon Odell, played by Jovan Adepo (The Odyssey, IT, Welcome to Derry, 3 Body Problem) back to the remote St. Amelia. Alongside them stars Kezia Burrows (Observation) in the role of Zoe, a compassionate nurse whose voice reaches out to Simon through layers of static on the CRTV.

The trailer also includes a glimpse at the horrors that await Simon, including relentless new monsters…

We have a new look at Ananta, the free-to-play urban open-world RPG from NetEase. Anime GTA, anyone? It's due out January 15, 2027 on Ananta's official PC client, on PC (Steam), PlayStation 5 and mobile platforms. Alongside the launch date announcement, Ananta's new trailer reveals Chongxiao, the game's second major city.

We got a brand new trailer for Gears of War: E-Day from Xbox. It's due out October 6.

We have a new Rainbow Six game! Rainbow Six Tactics is a new single-player, turn-based tactical game set in the Rainbow Six universe from Ubisoft Paris. It's due out 2027 across PC through Ubisoft Connect, Steam and the Epic Games Store, but also on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. It will also be available on Ubisoft+, GeForce Now, and Blacknut at launch. Much more on Rainbow Six Tactics here .

HoYoverse, developer of Genshin Impact, has announced a Monster Hunter / Elden Ring type game that is very different from what we're used to from the company. It's called Nodus Fall.

Geoff Keighley is on-stage, greeting the audience. There's plenty of applause. We're set for two hours of video game updates. "We've got a lot of great stuff for you today," Keighley says. articles.title: Avengers: Endgame Re-Release Reveals New Iron Man and Infinity Gauntlet Popcorn Buckets, Tickets On Sale Now
articles.summary: The upcoming re-release of Avengers: Endgame will coincide with the debut of two flashy new popcorn buckets.
articles.body:
The upcoming re-release of Avengers: Endgame will coincide with the debut of two flashy new popcorn buckets.

In 2019, Avengers: Endgame was released, but this was just before the big popcorn bucket craze. Now, every movie needs to have an absurd, expensive popcorn bucket themed after something in the film. The upcoming re-release of the MCU film will allow fans the chance to purchase an Iron Man helmet popcorn bucket or one based on Iron Man's version of the Infinity Gauntlet, which he uses to sacrifice himself and kill Thanos. The Iron Man helmet also projects a message that reads, "I love you 3,000."

Tickets are now on sale for the Avengers: Endgame re-release. The film hits theaters on September 25 and will include roughly five minutes of new footage , which will lead directly into Avengers: Doomsday . Marvel is keeping a tight lid on what exactly this new footage will feature, but it may introduce Doctor Doom or tee up what happens with Captain America after his "happy ending" in Endgame. Chris Evans is set to reprise his role as Steve Rogers in Doomsday and most likely Avengers: Secret Wars, as well.

Marvel is also boasting its new "Infinity Vision" branding for the re-release of Endgame . Avengers: Doomsday will not be getting an IMAX release when it debuts in December, so Marvel and Disney created a marketing initative known as Infinity Vision which will help promote the most "ideal" theaters for the film. It's not a new format, but a certification that elevates auditoriums that meet a quality standard held by Disney and Marvel.

Avengers: Endgame's re-release will allow fans to take advantage of Infinity Vision screens, but it will be released in IMAX, too. There's a chance that Doomsday will still get an IMAX release , as Spider-Man: Brand New Day got a delayed IMAX release and it wasn't promoted ahead of time. It led to viewers going back for repeat viewings, and it wouldn't be surprising if Doomsday employs a similar strategy in early 2027, once Dune's IMAX exclusivity is over.

articles.summary: The full Adventure Time Blu-ray set is now up for preorder with a release date of October 20, and the best deal is getting it directly through Gruv.
articles.body:
One of the best cartoons of all time is finally getting the full Blu-ray treatment.

Adventure Time originally aired from 2010 and 2018 and quickly became one of the most acclaimed cartoons in history. While all of the individual seasons have been released on Blu-ray, the full series has only been available in a standard DVD format in North America. Until now.

The full Adventure Time Blu-ray set is now up for preorder with a release date of October 20, and the best deal is getting it directly through Gruv .

Adventure Time Blu-ray Releasing October 20

Adventure Time: The Complete Series (Blu-ray)

Pricing currently varies across retailers, with Amazon listing the full set at $89.99 while it’s only $74.99 at Walmart and Gruv. The cheaper price likely has something to do with Gruv being the direct storefront for Warner Bros., the parent company of Cartoon Network. Amazon does offer a preorder pricing guarantee and will likely eventually price-match the other retailers , but for now, why not save a couple of bucks?

While the Amazon listing doesn’t have an image, Walmart and Gruv listings seem to confirm the new release will have the same green packaging as the existing DVD release, just with the Blu-ray logo tacked on the side. Speaking of, IGN did review the Season 1 Blu-ray over a decade ago, claiming "the conversion to Blu is impeccable." I'd imagine this new set will match that colorful quality.

The new set includes all 10 seasons of Adventure Time, a whopping 283 episodes. Instead of the standard DVD with 22 discs, the new Blu-ray set consolidates those episodes down to 12 discs. It also comes with the same spread of bonus features, including:

A retrospective documentary with the cast and crew

A documentary on the music of Adventure Time

We consistently praised all 10 seasons of Adventure Time, and ultimately gave the show’s final episode a perfect 10/10 .

While the original series ended back in 2018, Adventure Time continues to get plenty of love and greenlights. The spin-off series Fionna and Cake ran for two seasons on HBO Max, while a new spin-off, Adventure Time: Side Quests, recently premiered on Hulu and Disney+. An Adventure Time movie is also currently in development at Cartoon Network

articles.title: Fans Pay Tribute to Dolly Parton After Country Music Legend Dies at 80
articles.summary: Country music icon, actress, and philanthropist Dolly Parton has died at 80 years old.
articles.body:
Country music icon, actress, and philanthropist Dolly Parton has died at 80 years old.

Her death was confirmed in a statement published by her family to Dolly’s official Instagram account on August 25, 2026.

“A rhinestone life that shone bright enough for the world to see, Dolly will forever stand as an inspiration not only through her timeless music and prolific songwriting, but also her wit, warmth, and kindness that made us all feel like family. Dolly Parton’s legacy is one of love, compassion, and resilience. With a seven-decade career, she inspired multiple generations of artists and fans with her music and an unwavering commitment to making the world a better place. Her songs will continue to resonate with people of all ages, and her philanthropic work will have a lasting impact,” her family said in a press release.

A small, private memorial service will be held for Dolly’s immediate family. Fans and friends are encouraged to remember her with posts on social media or by leaving a message on her official website.

In lieu of flowers, Dolly’s family encourages fans to make donations to the singer’s Imagination Library , a program that mails free books to children from birth until they begin school in participating areas.

Dolly had been public with her physical health struggles over the last few months. Just three days ago, she spoke with PEOPLE , saying she had been "dealing with some health issues" that she "just didn't pay attention to" while she was caring for her late husband, Carl Thomas Dean.

“It’s not like I haven’t been through hard times with my health,” Parton told the outlet. "But I think because we live in a 24/7 world with social media, everything gets magnified in ways it wasn’t years ago. I used to joke that I was the Queen of the Tabloids, but now I guess I can say I’m the Queen of Social Media AI! Seriously, though, even though I’m still healin’, I’m still workin’.”

And in May, Dolly gave fans a health update in a video on her Instagram account, saying she was "responding really well to meds and treatments" and was "improving every day."

It's difficult to overstate Dolly's impact on the world. She first debuted on The Cas Walker Show in 1956 at just ten years old, going on to be an icon of the 60s and 70s with a sparkling discography that carried on well into the 80s, 90s, and 2000s.

Aside from her prolific music career, Dolly was also an actress, best known for her 1980 comedy 9 to 5 and, of course, her role as Miley Cyrus' fictional godmother in Disney's Hannah Montana sitcom.

Parton was a philanthropist through and through; on top of her Imagination Library program, she also ran The Dollywood Foundation , a non-profit organization that offers academic scholarships, community aid, and disaster relief.

Dolly Parton was an icon and an inspirational figure to many, and her life served as a shining example of how we should live and conduct ourselves. May we all be as kind, generous, and gentle as Miss Dolly.

articles.body:
Ubisoft has announced Rainbow Six Tactics, an upcoming single-player turn-based tactics game featuring familiar Rainbow Six Siege Operators. Revealed at Gamescom's Opening Night Live showcase, and is due out in 2027 for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S. It's the first single-player game in the franchise since Rainbow Six Vegas 2 for the Xbox 360 and PS3 in 2008.

And speaking of Rainbow Six Vegas, you play as Vegas protagonist Paul "Six" Bishop in Tactics, who will command the Operators from afar. Tactics will feature 15 fan-favorite Operators from Siege, including Sledge and Ash, and it's packing 47 total handcrafted maps along with 90 minutes of cutscenes to support the narrative. It's set during the collapse of Rainbow between Siege's 10th and 11th years. Development is being led by Ubisoft Paris, makers of fellow tactics game Mario + Rabbids as well as the last several Ghost Recon games (speaking of which, it's high-time for a new Ghost Recon game if you ask me!). Ubisoft also told IGN that there is no in-game store and no monetizations.

Rainbow Six Tactics includes a breach planning feature – which might trigger a memory for fans of the original Rainbow Six on PC from back in 1998 – allowing you to plan and execute synchronized assaults with your Operators. Check back later today for our exclusive interview with R6 Tactics game director Martial Potron.

articles.title: Tides of Annihilation Trailer Confirms Resident Evil Requiem Actress Angela Sant'Albano as New Voice of Gwendolyn
articles.summary: Tides of Annihilation has confirmed Resident Evil Requiem actress Angela Sant'Albano as the new voice of Gwendolyn.
articles.body:
Tides of Annihilation has confirmed Resident Evil Requiem actress Angela Sant'Albano as the new voice of Gwendolyn.

Eclipse Glow Games announced the news at gamescom Opening Night Live (ONL) 2026. It came with a new trailer for the highly anticipated Arthurian action-RPG, giving Tides of Annihilation fans a taste of Sant'Albano's new take on Gwendolyn.

"In the trailer, a distraught Gwendolyn considers her new reality amidst the ash of a ruinous London before being encouraged by the legendary Guinevere to harness the power of the Fog - a power only King Arthur once wielded - to save both London and the otherworldly realm of Avalon from total annihilation," an official description said. "Embracing her destiny, Gwendolyn takes up the sword and learns to fight alongside powerful spectral knights; this new trailer debuts the legendary Sir Lancelot summoned by Gwendolyn to dispatch enemies in spectacular style."

Sant'Albano is a star with a resume that includes parts in The Nevers, and Disney's live-action Dumbo movie, but the gaming world is still celebrating her for the part she played in Resident Evil Requiem. She showed up in Capcom's ninth mainline installment as Grace Ashcroft, a newcomer to the series with a shaky voice and deadly aim.

Despite half of the last Resident Evil being carried by fan-favorite zombie-slayer Leon S. Kennedy, Sant'Albano helped Grace emerge as yet another one of the series' memorable characters. Now, she's officially set to help do the same for Tides of Annihilation.

"I am beyond thrilled—and deeply honored—to officially announce that I’m stepping into the role of Gwendolyn in Tides of Annihilation," Sant'Albano said in a statement. "Gwen is the kind of heroine I love. She carries self-doubt, constantly questioning whether she's enough, but she refuses to let fear make her stand still. Everything she does is driven by love for her sister and her homeland, and I think that's what makes her strength feel so human. Getting to step into her boots, facing otherworldly demigods, and commanding Knights of the Round Table has been an absolute privilege."

Sant'Albano is officially joining the cast of another game that has players excited, but her part may not come as a shock to those who have kept up with all of the updates. When former Gwendolyn actress Jennifer English announced she would be stepping away from the role due to health concerns, rumors about who would take her place immediately began to spread.

The Resident Evil Requiem star was one of the first names to spread among fans. When some fans noticed some character models had seemingly been changed , rumors only heated up.

Eclipse Glow has also announced Tides of Annihilation will support Brazilian Portuguese when it eventually launches. That brings its supported languages up to 11, including English, French, Italian, German, Spanish, Japanese, Chinese Simplified, Chinese Traditional, Korean, Russian. Additionally, gamescom attendees have been told that they'll be able to enjoy a hands-on demo.

Tides of Annihilation currently has no release date but is expected to launch for PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. During gamescom's Opening Night Live , developer Archetype Entertainment revealed the release date for its Mass Effect-like spacefaring RPG: Exodus is launching on April 7, 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam and Epic Games Store. It premiered a new cinematic trailer that showcased new characters and gameplay centered around an intelligent octopus who pilots a mech suit.

Her name is Salt and she is one of several party members you'll gather in Exodus. She is an Awakened, which in the universe of Exodus are hyper-intelligent animals and wildlife who can communicate with humans. Salt will be a long-range sniper who can use an ink smokescreen to provide cover in combat. The trailer hits heavier beats that tease some of its story elements – while Salt gives the main character Jun hard time and tends to be confrontational, she's emotionally driven to protect her species and homeworld.

One of the major hooks of Exodus is the scientific incorporation of time dilation and how it'll affect the story. In true RPG fashion, it'll have player choices that can change outcomes and you'll have a crew to accompany you (a Traveler known as Jun) along the interstallar journey where humanity had to flee Earth and find a new home in the great expanse.

Veteran narrative designer and writer Drew Karpyshyn is the narrative director on Exodus. If you're not familiar, he worked on some of BioWare's most critically acclaimed games serving as senior writer on Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic and lead writer on Mass Effect.

Exodus was first revealed during The Game Awards 2023 and made headlines for having famed actor Matthew McCounghey voicing the trailer and playing a character in the game. There was an extended 20-minute gameplay reveal back in June that showcased the action RPG combat, which is very reminescent of Mass Effect with its shooting mechanics and commanding of party member abilities – it also shares a particular sci-fi aesthetic with the BioWare series. Archtype Entertainment has been working under Wizards of the Coast since 2020 and it won't be long until we can finally play what its been working on.

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Commodore Computer Premieres at Gamescom, and It's Up for Preorder Now
articles.summary: The retro-futurism of Cyberpunk 2077 meets the retro computerism of the modern Commodore 64.
articles.body:
When I reviewed the Commodore 64 Ultimate, I honestly couldn't believe just how perfect it was. It surprised me in ways I didn't expect, and it's truly the result of a love and respect for the brand. It's why I gave the C64 Ultimate a 10 in my review . It's a thing of beauty, and now Commodore has officially unveiled a gorgeous new update in collaboration with CD Projekt Red: The Commodore 77.

The case itself is gorgeous, with the plate on the function keys now made of brushed metal. That's not a "brushed metal" finish, by the way: it's actually brushed metal. The rest of the case has been colored to match the Cyberpunk style, the Commodore 64 badge has been replaced with a Commodore 77 badge, and there are other changes that have to be seen to really be appreciated. The entire case has a weathered, suitably cyberpunk look to it, but just like with humans, it's what's inside that counts.

Aside from the new look, the Commodore 77 can now run at a blistering 77Mhz, compared to the 1Mhz of the original Commodore 64. There's also 77MB of system RAM compared to the original Ultimate's 16MB. While this new speed and power is pretty impressive (for the 1980s), it does run the risk of making some of your hand-written programs run impossibly fast, but you can toggle the higher speed off and on in the menus.

Hey, speaking of menus, the C77 also has a "custom Cyberpunk 2077 themed Commodore 77 BASIC 2.0 boot screen", which continues the overall Cyberpunk feel. The famous spiral-bound manual that's shipped with each Commodore 64 has also gotten a Cyberpunk facelift, and comes "packed with lore and exclusive Cyberpunk 2077-themed type-in BASIC programs." It's exactly the kind of thing old heads like me crave.

Each Commodore 77 ships with a shard-inspired Arasaka cartridge containing a demo created by Polish demo group Arise, with the soundtrack composed by chiptune artist LukHash. This is an old-school computer demo, the sort of thing hackers used to distribute to show off their chops. I've seen it. It's incredible. It's hard to believe what people can do with such limited computational power, but the soundtrack benefits enormously from the 24-track stereo SID chip that's part of the Ultimate.

Given how well Commodore did with its modern debut, I have no doubt in my mind the C77 is going to be similarly awesome, especially given the pedigree of its collaboration. Did I mention it comes with stickers and pins and in "collectible themed packaging?"

Oh, and it has LED lights that dance to the music on the demo. It's kind of everything I didn't even know I wanted.

Preorders are live at Commodore's website for $377, with an expected release date sometime next year. I, for one, welcome our CyberPunk and Commodore retro future.

Backrooms officially has a streaming release date.

The breakout horror movie directed by 21-year-old-Kane Parsons is coming to HBO Max on Friday, September 25. It will debut on HBO linear channels the following day at 8pm ET.

The streaming release comes just under four months after Backrooms was initially released in theaters, where it dominated the box office. It grossed over $80 million in its opening weekend and quickly become A24’s highest-grossing movie of all time . It finished its theatrical run at just shy of $400 million globally , and remains one of the highest-grossing movies of the year so far .

Toward the end of its stint in theaters, Backrooms received became available to watch in extended “Everything Must Go” screenings, featuring over 15 minutes of extra footage in the style of Parsons’ original YouTube series. That extra footage is already available to watch on YouTube for free , and it's unclear whether it'll be added to HBO Max in any capacity.

For now, Backrooms is available to rent or buy digitally from platforms like Prime Video. A spread of 4K Blu-rays with "over three hours of special features" are also available to buy from the A24 Shop .

We were pretty big fans of Backrooms, with critic Lex Briscuso describing it as “a truly terrifying cinematic rabbit hole” in her 8/10 review for IGN . It's one of our best-reviewed movies of the year so far, and generally currently sits at an 87% rating on Rotten Tomatoes .

All in all, it should come as no surprise that there are already talks of a potential sequel , though Parsons has also expressed his interest in adapting the iconic 2007 Valve game, Portal. Other creepypasta-inspired movies have also been getting the green light since the Backrooms success, most notably a Siren Head movie helmed by Weapons ' and the upcoming Resident Evil movie's director, Zach Cregger.

articles.body:
A new LEGO city builder known as LEGO Skylines has been announced at Gamescom.

After a leak earlier this summer , Paradox Interactive has officially announced a LEGO version of its beloved city builder series, Cities: Skylines. Developed by Iceflake Studios, LEGO Skylines aims to allow players to build functional and logical cities, as you would in other city builders, but also push them to make something more creative and whimsical. One such example provided by the team behind the game is putting a bakery on every corner of the city, which can produce donuts using wheat provided by farmers from elsewhere in your city.

Using the creativity and imagination of the LEGO brand, LEGO Skylines players will be able to build the city of their dreams — not just maintain a realistic, functioning city, but one that lets them try outlandish and absurd ideas using LEGO bricks and decorations. The game promises a "frankly absurd amount of buildings, decorations, and other cool stuff" to build cities.

“Building and creativity have always been at the heart of the LEGO experience, but LEGO Skylines takes us into completely new territory,” said Fredrik Löving, SVP, Global Head of game at the LEGO Group. “Together with Paradox Interactive and Iceflake Studios, we have brought the LEGO experience to one of the world's most beloved gaming genres. From the beginning, our ambition wasn’t just to make a LEGO city-builder, it was to create a game that is considered among the best in the genre. Whether players dream of building a bustling metropolis, a quirky seaside town, or something nobody has imagined before, LEGO Skylines gives them the creative freedom and depth to make it happen.”

All in all, it sounds like a really charming and fun city builder. There's no release date for LEGO Skylines at the moment, but it will be available on Xbox Series X|S, PS5, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC when it comes out.

articles.title: Roco Kingdom Goes Global
articles.body:
Since its launch in China in March 2026, Roco Kingdom has made a huge mark on the country's app charts. The game went straight to the top among new mobile titles, both in terms of average daily active users and revenue. Revealed at Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026, Morefun Studios will be bringing this hugely popular Chinese franchise to the rest of the world with their first global closed beta test on 27th October.

If you've never heard of Roco Kingdom, that's because the franchise has spent most of its 16-year life in China, where it's seen huge success. What started as a browser game in 2010 has since spawned four feature films, a long-running animated series, and over 100 published books. The game itself has had more than 350 million registered players across its history.

Roco Kingdom is a multiplayer open-world creature-collecting game where players take on the role of a Roco, setting out to explore the sprawling continent of Carosia to befriend its native creatures, called Jinies. There are over 400+ of them at launch, and no two are quite the same: every Jini has its own unique height, weight, and habits, interacting with the world around them in ways that make the environment feel variable and dynamic.

Developed by Morefun Studios, known for extraction shooter Arena Breakout: Infinite, the latest game has been in development for the last six years. The world itself is built around natural habitats, with distinct landscapes and climates shaping where different Jini species live and behave with the outcome being a living ecosystem rather than a static backdrop.

Meet, Bond, and Journey Together With Friends

The creature-collecting loop will feel familiar to anyone who's spent time with the genre: discover Jinies in the wild, catch them, and build a roster. But Roco Kingdom’s 16-year heritage allows it to build on its significant foundations. The social systems here go beyond simply trading and battling: players can decorate and farm their own home spaces, visit friends' setups, and hop on shared rides together through the world. Cross-platform play is supported, meaning PC players and mobile players can journey through Carosia side by side.

With regards to the PvP system, whilst the game is free-to-play, Morefun Studios are at pains to state that this isn’t simply a case of pay to win. Every Jini is obtainable through gameplay, and the competitive meta is built entirely around strategy; type matchups, team composition, and roster diversity rather than just how much you've spent.

If you’d like to get a taste of the full kingdom, check out their reveal trailer here:

Roco Kingdom launches its first closed beta test on 27th October, on PC, iOS and Android. Registration is now open via rocokingdom.com . Stay tuned to IGN as more about the game is revealed in the coming months.

articles.title: 1001 Threads of Mizan: The First Preview
articles.summary: While I can definitely see it working well solo, playing with two other players in real time is where 1001 Threads of Mizan really shines. There were no multiplayer quick time events or big flashy mid-fight cutscenes that triggered when everyone did a specific thing, but there were definitely moments where all three of us needed to attack a single weak point, or work together to defeat various obstacles at once in different areas during the boss fight. I'm very interested to see how this fusion of single-player and co-op works throughout the game.
articles.body:
GTA 6 isn’t even out yet and 2026 has already been a great year for video games. From this spring's outstanding Resident Evil Requiem to surprises like Denshattack, Mina The Hollower, and other games like 007, Life is Strange Reunion, Marathon… you get the point. This year has been awesome, so the bar is a little high for me when it comes to playing something original from a brand new studio like MBC. 1001 Threads of Mizan is a completely original title from a new studio led by a plethora of industry veterans who are looking to make something that not only brings the world and stories of One Thousand and One Nights to an action-adventure game, but also create something that plays as fun as it looks. And from my short time with iit, fighting two bosses and zipping around on a magic carpet, I can definitely see the vision — and in an era of games that are constantly redefining what it means to be great, 1001 Threads of Mizan is looking pretty promising.

From the very start of my demo it was obvious that 1001 Threads of Mizan’s developer MBC Game Studio is taking its source material seriously in an effort to make something that’s unique and interesting. After the intro cutscene, there was barely any chatter between the three main characters, and most of the world-building and story was handled by a narrator, Shahrazad, who is the actual storyteller in the book One Thousand and One Nights that 1001 Threads of Mizan is based on. 1001 Threads is rich with its source material, and it was great seeing an action-adventure game take place in a time period that isn't really covered that often in AAA games.

But story isn't everything, and in my short time with 1001 Threads of Mizan, it was obvious that the gameplay falls somewhere between Kingdom Hearts’ fast-paced and flashy combat and a souls-like approach to pattern recognition and dodging. Mizan is a really fun game, and in my demo I was able to fight numerous Jinn enemies, as well as two interesting and surprisingly challenging boss battles. One of which took a bit more teamwork to take down than I had anticipated, which was really fun and took me back to the good ol’ days of couch co-op games with my friends.

In my demo, I was given a choice between three distinct characters who play within their classes. Yusra is based on more long-range weapons and attacks, while Malik is your typical heavy who deals high damage at close range and can be a bit of a tank, while Sufyan plays a bit faster. I chose Sufyan and immediately figured out his playstyle without the need of a complicated tutorial system or overbearing menus. Everything just seemed to click, and I never had to take a beat to figure out how to play the game. The combat felt tight and responsive, dodging and blocking felt natural, and managing my special attack meter was easy and quickly became second nature.

1001 Threads of Mizan - First Screenshots

The real star of the show here, though, is the ability to auto-summon a magic carpet anywhere and zip around the environment. This was great to use in combat if I needed to get away from the action to recover, get closer to an enemy's weak spot, or just use it to help juggle aerial combos and perform team-based attacks. The magic carpet, like Mizan's combat, just works. It's not overly complicated, it can be summoned with one button, and there was never a moment where I felt like the carpet was moving too fast or clunky. In short, it's a really fun way to move around.

I was told by the game’s directors that 1001 Threads of Mizan is at its core a single-player experience that features a drop-in and drop-out multiplayer aspect. While I can definitely see it working well solo, playing with two other players in real time is where 1001 Threads really shines. There were no multiplayer quick time events or big flashy mid-fight cutscenes that triggered when everyone did a specific thing, but there were definitely moments where all three of us needed to attack a single weak point, or work together to defeat various obstacles at once in different areas during the boss fight. I'm very interested to see how this fusion of single-player and co-op works throughout the game.

In my short time with 1001 Threads of Mizan, it was obvious that this is definitely something worth keeping on your radar thanks to its intuitive and fun combat, a unique take on One Thousand and One Nights, and its take on making a game work as a single-player and multiplayer narrative experience. We’ll have to see how things shake out, but if MBC Game Studio can pull it off, 1001 Threads of Mizan could definitely be one of the most pleasant gaming surprises in quite a while.

articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day Campaign Hands-On Preview: To Quote Marcus Fenix, “Nice”
articles.summary: I’m now not only more fired up to finish Gears of War: E-Day’s prequel story than ever, but I’m also more confident than ever that, at least based on the small slice I’ve played so far, E-Day has struck the exact right balance of tried-and-true old stuff and compelling new stuff.
articles.body:
Playing the beginning of Act 2 of Gears of War: E-Day's campaign immediately gave me a healthy dose of everything I love about Gears of War.

Weapon and combat mechanics have been nicely evolved through the weapon mod system.

Gears 5's open-world aspects have been reined in with something smarter: a multi-path downtown area with optional secondary objectives and plenty of hidden collectibles.

[ Editor's Note : Mild spoilers ahead for E-Day’s campaign, so turn back now if you don’t want to know any more…]

I’m a massive fan of Gears of War, as I have been since the very beginning. But I have to be honest: something about Gears of War: E-Day’s campaign reveal at the Xbox Showcase a couple months ago just didn’t quite land right with me. It wasn’t bad, by any stretch of the imagination. But I just wasn’t as fired up as I thought I’d be after seeing the first new Gears of War campaign footage in seven years (OK, six if we’re counting Hivebusters).

When I finally sat down to play E-Day’s campaign, though, it took all of about 30 seconds to turn my tepid feelings into joyful smiles. My one-hour preview, which covered the early parts of Act 2, featured plenty of everything I want from and love about Gears of War: Marcus Fenix, Dominic Santiago, lots of story cutscenes, a sweet mix of old weapons and new ones (including the origin story for a signature Gears firearm known for its sharp teeth), some evolved gameplay mechanics, killer setpieces, new Marcus Fenix one-liners, subtle references to characters we know and love, and did I mention Marcus Fenix saying and doing cool sh*t?

I was so fired up by what I played that when I got hit with the “demo complete” screen it actually hurt. I suppose The Coalition got the reaction it wanted from me, because all I wanted to do was keep going. And I’m now not only more fired up to finish Gears of War: E-Day’s prequel story than ever, but I’m also more confident than ever that, at least based on the small slice I’ve played so far, E-Day has struck the exact right balance of tried-and-true old stuff and compelling new stuff.

Act 2 picks up with Marcus and Dom still in their civvies, scavenged Mark-1 Lancers in hand. They’ve arrived with fellow civilian-dressed COG soldiers Carter and Reyes at a makeshift command center with the mayor of Kolona, whom they’ve no doubt rescued in Act 1. COG officer Colonel Trench and the mayor face off about whatever the heck is happening out there – you and I both know darn well what it is, of course – and how best to handle it, leading the angry Colonel to yell at our heroes to get some armor on. And then Awesome Moment #1 happens: Marcus and Dom suit up in their familiar COG garb, flanked by Carter and Reyes in the newly christened Bravo Squad. “Guess we’re back to it,” Marcus says, and he might as well be speaking for players as well. My grin could not have been any wider.

Venturing out into the city of Kolona, we see ash raining from a cloudy sky and remnants of once-proud buildings around us. This moment definitely hearkens back to the “destroyed beauty” aesthetic of Gears 1. We soon find our way to the heart of this chapter of gameplay: a massive suspension bridge that raises and lowers in multiple sections in order to let large ships pass underneath it. All of that was in the Before Times, of course, before actual Hell started erupting from the ground beneath the people of this city. We’re making our way towards Oria Stadium, home of the Kolona Eagles thrashball team, where civilians are being routed to in the event of the citywide disaster. But we’re going to have to fight our way there.

This straight-ahead bridge section certainly isn’t the combat bowls we’re used to with Gears, but it’s a great way to warm up – not to mention climb up, meaning: to get a feel for using E-Day’s new verticality, i.e. you can now mantle up and over cover, including the cars that the Locust are using to shield themselves. The Mark-1 Lancer, Gnasher shotgun, Snub pistol, and frag grenades all work exactly as you remember them. Gears of War’s core combat has aged remarkably well over the past 20 years. However, E-Day introduces a welcome new evolution in the form of unlockable weapon mods. Each firearm has four total mod slots, and mods vary by weapon, of course. Every reloadable weapon, by default, gets the classic damage bonus if you nail a perfect reload; it’s called Full Metal Jacket now. But there’s a heck of a lot more than just that. For instance, on the aforementioned Gnasher – which, yes, is still your best point-blank bet for turning low-level Locust Drones into chunky-style soup – has an Auto Pouch mod that automatically reloads the shotgun when you stow it (i.e. switch weapons).

This also seems like a good time to mention the new Tactical Gear, which I unlocked at the very end of my demo build. (You got to experience these in the Versus beta weekend, if you participated.) These are short-duration (45-second) buffs with a cooldown, and they also have unlockable mod slots, none of which were available in the preview. But even without mods, the Adrenaline Injector immediately refills your health when triggered and also increases your damage dealt while decreasing damage taken. Choosing the Sonic Disruptor Tactical Gear, meanwhile, nets you a more defensive bonus: stunning low-level enemies in a cone in front of you, interrupting their attacks. With tons more of all of these left to unlock over the course of the campaign, they should add a welcome bit of personalization and gameplay customization to your playthroughs – emphasis on plural there, because I’ll be shocked if there isn’t a New Game+ available that lets you run the campaign again with all of your Tactical Gear and weapon mods available from the jump on higher difficulties.

After battling our way up and across the massive Allfather’s Legacy Bridge, including fending off a couple of Boomers along the way and getting some reps in with the Breechshot (last seen in Gears of War: Judgment), we arrived at Oria Stadium, where the COG was coordinating a stressful civilian rescue operation, with lines of the city’s residents waiting to be processed and allowed into the massive facility. We entered and caught up with the quartermaster, Russ, who took a liking to Marcus because he knew his father, Adam. He asked what Bravo Squad needed, and after Marcus complained about the bayonets easily breaking off of the Mark-1 Lancers, that’s when one of the COG in our party set the chainsaw used to save Marcus’ life in Act 1, as seen in the Xbox Showcase demo, on the table. The quartermaster looks at the chainsaw with a twinkle in his eye, and, yeah…you can probably see where this is going. Awesome Moment #2: Marcus and Bravo Squad get handed the first prototype Mark-2 Lancers with chainsaw built right in. Again, the smile on my face was almost Joker-like.

We headed out from the stadium with the goal of getting across the downtown section of the city to the train station. It’s here that Awesome Moment #3 began to unfold: environmental freedom. The linear path of the bridge we’d fought across had finally given way to a larger combat space. This seems to deliberately rein in Gears 5’s huge open-world areas by instead giving you room to clear Kalona’s streets block-by-block in whatever order and fashion you choose. It’s a smaller-scale version of what we got in the last game, but based on my initial impression, it’s a more effective one. In fact, I ran through the preview build again to take a different route through Kolona, and I’m glad I did. This approach also allows for higher hidden-collectible potential (because yes, of course there are collectibles in a Gears campaign). I also enjoyed the optional secondary objectives in this section that you can opt into. In one, a family was trapped inside a convenience store, and I had to fight off a wave of Wretches before finding a way inside to free them and radio in to get them an escort to the stadium.

This was also when E-Day introduced Supply Caches, which will be scattered throughout the city and allow you to change out your weapons and mods. It’s an organic and straightforward way of letting you change up weapons on the fly without having to kill an enemy to get what you’re after.

Don’t Need No Credit Card to Ride This Train

The all-too-soon end of my demo came in the Octus Way train station. This was a pretty sizable combat bowl, with three levels of verticality to contend with plus a left, right, and center area of the room to be keeping an eye on, lest the Locust manage to flank you from the side or from behind. It was a frantic but not overwhelming fight; we didn’t face off against the Corpser that was teased while we were clearing Kolona city blocks on our way to the train station, meaning that encounter is no doubt waiting for us later. But Octus Way Station was a good chance to try out all of the weapons (thanks to the Supply Cache in the corner of the upstairs entrance) and rev up the Lancer’s chainsaw for a few good ol’ fashioned Locust executions. Once I loaded up and stepped out of the cleared-out train station, that’s when I got the aforementioned “demo complete” message and reluctantly put down my controller.

One final note: as I mentioned, I ran through the preview twice – once on Performance graphics mode, and once on the 30fps Quality graphics mode. The latter was not running well on Xbox Series X in the preview build. It wasn’t unplayably bad by any means, but it was noticeably sub-30 in a lot of spots. I expect most people will opt for Performance mode anyway, but it’s worth noting and hoping that The Coalition is able to squeeze a few extra fps out of it in the remaining few weeks of development.

That minor complaint aside, I can’t say enough about how much I loved what I’ve played of Gears of War: E-Day’s campaign so far. Does it completely rewrite the rules of Gears? No, but I don’t think anyone – myself included – is looking for that. Besides, this prequel was never about that. It’s about getting Marcus and Dom back together and getting Gears back to its roots. And in the incredibly short slice I’ve seen so far, it absolutely accomplishes that with the highest of marks. I am now chock-full of the hype that the Xbox Showcase demo failed to give me. In the words of Marcus Fenix, sweet .

While you're here, check out these previews of other big upcoming games we've played recently!
